ageing_relevance.rationale: About 10% of B2M papers concern ageing and 5% senescence, and it is a GrimAge component. Open Targets lists no age-related disease associations. The project finding concerns the DNAm surrogate, not measured protein.

evidence.value: One of seven plasma proteins whose DNA-methylation surrogates make up the GrimAge clock. Part 1 of this project: the GrimAge clock as a whole was +4.3 years older in schizophrenia, a difference that disappeared after adjusting for a methylation smoking score; this protein's own surrogate was not tested. Surrogates are methylation estimates, not measured protein levels. Shirai et al. 2024 (7-cohort meta-analysis): this protein's DNAm surrogate was higher in schizophrenia or first-episode psychosis in a model adjusted for age, sex and DNAm smoking pack-years.

background_knowledge: Mouse parabiosis work (Smith et al. 2015) linked raised circulating B2M to impaired neurogenesis and cognition; plasma B2M rises with age in humans.

mechanism.rationale: B2M's function is well characterised as the MHC class I light chain. Its causal role in ageing is less clear. Inhibiting circulating B2M is plausible, but it would conflict with its essential immune role.

evidence.value: Component of the class I major histocompatibility complex (MHC). Involved in the presentation of peptide antigens to the immune system.

background_knowledge: Pro-ageing effects of circulating B2M come from preclinical mouse studies; human causal evidence is limited.

tractability.rationale: There is small-molecule evidence (structure with ligand, high-quality pocket), antibody evidence (secreted or cell-surface) and PROTAC evidence. No approved-drug precedent is shown.

safety.rationale: Open Targets lists no safety liabilities, but absence of data is not evidence of safety. Disease associations show that loss of B2M causes MHC class I deficiency, so broad inhibition risks immune impairment. B2M is also linked to lymphoma and viral infection.
background_knowledge: Complete B2M loss abolishes MHC class I surface expression, which impairs CD8 T-cell and NK-cell function.

clinical_precedence.rationale: No drugs targeting B2M are listed in the clinic.

assessment.summary: B2M is the secreted MHC class I light chain and a component of the GrimAge clock. About 10% of its literature concerns ageing, but Open Targets lists no age-related disease associations. The project finding applies only to its DNAm surrogate, which was higher in schizophrenia or first-episode psychosis. It has small-molecule, antibody and PROTAC tractability evidence but no clinical candidates. Safety data are empty, but the MHC class I deficiency association signals an immune risk from systemic inhibition. Recommendation: consider.
key_uncertainties: Whether lowering circulating B2M slows ageing in humans (causal evidence is missing).
Whether selective inhibition of circulating B2M is possible without impairing MHC class I function.
Whether measured B2M protein, not just its DNAm surrogate, differs in schizophrenia or ageing.
source_conflicts: Literature shows about 10% of papers on ageing, but Open Targets lists 0 ageing disease associations. I relied on both and scored ageing relevance moderate.
Tractability shows small-molecule, antibody and PROTAC evidence, but there are no clinical candidates. I scored tractability on the evidence and clinical precedence as none.
Open Targets lists 0 safety liabilities, but the top disease association is MHC class I deficiency. I scored safety conservatively.
